Assuming class called custom, methods named fm_dof.custom() fm_basis.custom(). fm_dof.custom(x) method must take object x class custom return number degrees freedom function space. fm_basis.custom(x, loc, ..., full = FALSE) method must take object x class custom return sparseMatrix Matrix matrix column containing basis function evaluated locations determined loc. type loc may type (types) supported custom class. ... part can include named arguments specific custom class. must optional arguments fm_basis(x, loc) works. full = TRUE, full fm_basis object must returned, list containing least basis matrix , logical vector, ok, indicating loc values valid evaluation points. matrix must -zero invalid loc. requirements fulfilled, default fm_evaluator() fm_evaluate() methods can used evaluate functions location, without need user define methods. what: Example: Harmonic function space of order n
title: Custom mesh classes
text: Note: version 0.2.0.9004, fm_basis.matrix, fm_basis.Matrix, fm_basis.list methods provide easier way construct fm_basis object, creating object optionally extracting single call:
code: # Custom class for harmonic functions up to order `n` create_custom <- function(n) {   stopifnot(n >= 0)   structure(     list(n = n),     class = "custom"   ) } fm_dof.custom <- function(x) {   # Return the number of degrees of freedom   1L + 2L * x[["n"]] } fm_basis.custom <- function(x, loc, ..., full = FALSE) {   # Return the evaluated basis functions   A <- Matrix::Matrix(0.0, NROW(loc), fm_dof(x))   ok <- !is.na(loc)   A[ok, 1L] <- 1.0   for (k in seq_len(x[["n"]])) {     A[ok, 2 * k] <- cos(2 * pi * k * loc[ok])     A[ok, 2 * k + 1L] <- sin(2 * pi * k * loc[ok])   }   result <- structure(     list(       A = A,       ok = ok, # Required prior to version 0.2.0.9003       loc = loc     ),     class = "fm_basis"   )    # Use the fm_basis method to extract the A matrix if full is FALSE:   fm_basis(result, full = full) } # 'matrix' and 'Matrix' methods: fm_basis(   A = A,   ok = ok, # If missing or NULL, inferred to be all TRUE   loc = loc, # Optional additional content   full = full ) # 'list' method: fm_basis(   list(     A = A,     ok = ok, # If missing or NULL, inferred to be all TRUE     loc = loc   ),   full = full )

title: Converting legacy INLA mesh code to fmesher
text: Three INLA::inla.getOption()/INLA::inla.setOption() options control transition behaviour INLA package use fmesher. fmesher.evolution, integer: 1L uses intermediate fm_* methods fmesher already available via inlabru 2.8.0, calls INLA built-fmesher standalone programme mesh construction related operations. (INLA version 23.06.29) 2L uses full range fmesher package methods, use standalone fmesher programme. (INLA around version 23.08.20, now supported option.) fmesher.evolution.warn, logical: TRUE, INLA show deprecation methods methods INLA replaced fmesher package methods. FALSE, warnings shown. Set option TRUE want update code, keep FALSE need run existing code without changing . fmesher.evolution.verbosity, character: Either “soft”, “warn”, “stop”, indicating minimum warning level fmesher.evolution.warn TRUE. text: fmesher package several features aren’t widely known. code started implementation triangulation method detailed Hjelle Dæhlen, “Triangulations Applications” (2006), includes methods spatially varying mesh quality.1 time, interface feature improvements focused robustness calculating useful mesh properties, advanced mesh quality features still ! algorithm first builds basic mesh, including points user specifies, well boundary curves (boundary curve given, default boundary added), connecting points Delaunay triangulation. initial step, mesh quality decided two criteria: Minimum allowed angle triangle Maximum allowed triangle edge length long triangle fulfil criteria, new mesh point added way guaranteed locally fix problem, new Delaunay triangulation obtained. process repeated triangles fulfil criteria. perfect arithmetic, algorithm guaranteed converge long minimum angle criterion 21 degrees, maximum edge length criterion strictly positive. basic mesh regular interior triangles can created follows:  fm_nonconvex_hull_inla function creates polygon used boundary mesh, extending domain distance convex given points, keeping outside curvature radius least concave. simple example, used method fm_rcdt_2d_inla, direct interface fmesher. refine = list(max.edge = Inf) setting makes fmesher enforce default minimum angle criterion (21 degrees) ignore edge length criterion. get smaller triangles, change max.edge value:  often possible desirable increase minimum allowed angle achieve smooth transitions small large triangles (values high 26 27, almost never high 35, may possible). instead focus edge length criterion, make spatially varying.

text: now define function computes desired maximal edge length function location, feed output fm_rcdt_2d_inla using quality.spec parameter instead max.edge:  gave smooth transition large small triangles! can also use different settings boundary, e.g. NA_real_ Inf make care edge lengths near boundary:  can also make complicated specifications, beware asking reasonable triangulations; experimenting, recommend setting max.n.strict max.n values refine parameter list, prohibits adding infinitely many triangles!
code: qual_loc <- function(loc) {   if (inherits(loc, c("sf", "sfc", "sfg"))) {     loc <- sf::st_coordinates(loc)   }   pmax(0.05, (loc[, 1] * 2 + loc[, 2]) / 16) } mesh3 <- fm_rcdt_2d_inla(   loc = loc,   boundary = bnd,   refine = list(max.edge = Inf),   quality.spec = list(     loc = qual_loc(loc),     segm = qual_loc(bnd$loc)   ) ) ggplot() +   geom_fm(data = mesh3) +   coord_sf(default = TRUE) qual_bnd <- function(loc) {   rep(Inf, nrow(loc)) } mesh5 <- fm_rcdt_2d_inla(   loc = loc,   boundary = bnd,   refine = list(max.edge = Inf),   quality.spec = list(     loc = qual_loc(loc),     segm = qual_bnd(bnd$loc)   ) ) ggplot() +   geom_fm(data = mesh5) +   coord_sf(default = TRUE) qual_bnd <- function(loc) {   if (inherits(loc, c("sf", "sfc", "sfg"))) {     loc <- sf::st_coordinates(loc)   }   pmax(0.1, 1 - abs(loc[, 2] / 10)^2) } mesh5 <- fm_rcdt_2d_inla(   loc = loc,   boundary = bnd,   refine = list(     max.edge = Inf,     max.n.strict = 5000   ),   quality.spec = list(     loc = qual_loc(loc),     segm = qual_bnd(bnd$loc)   ) ) ggplot() +   geom_fm(data = mesh5) +   coord_sf(default = TRUE)
